differences.description: The opening detail shows a more opaque, uniformly gridded GPT surface with a dark red crest and sharply resolved mesh. GPT renders the Supervised and Unsupervised names in pale text; ORIGINAL colors those names orange and cyan respectively. The colored rules remain, but part of the classification's color coding is lost.

Across 11–16 seconds, GPT presents a more rectangular, flatter projected terrain patch. Its crest sits farther left, its rear edge is more horizontal and its cyan hollow lacks the clearly exposed underside seen in ORIGINAL. Consequently, the crest leader is nearly vertical rather than diagonal, and the trough callout follows a different silhouette.

Across the descent samples, GPT's terrain pose places the crest farther left and raises the right rear corner more strongly. At 29 seconds, the full-resolution pair shows a distinctly steeper diagonal right boundary and a different basin projection. The matching counters therefore accompany visibly different ball and route positions.

ORIGINAL's front rim hides the descent endpoint and part of the orange directional arrow; a teal underside remains visible below it. GPT leaves the white endpoint sphere fully exposed above the basin and does not reproduce that rim/arrow relationship. The route also reads as dark, shaded orange beads rather than ORIGINAL's brighter, softer markers.

GPT's loss chart has a conspicuous angular early bend and long straight segments. ORIGINAL's curve descends more smoothly and has a clearer cyan terminal section. The displayed step and loss values agree.

The learning-rate legend builds later in GPT. At 35 seconds, ORIGINAL shows the white and cyan rows with the orange row beginning to appear; GPT shows only the white row. All three are present by 36 seconds.

Across 36–42 seconds, GPT compresses the learning-rate demonstration into a shallower terrain view with a higher front rim. Its cyan markers form a mostly upright cluster near the trough, whereas ORIGINAL shows more lateral separation among cyan sphere positions and trail segments. GPT's white and orange routes also share a flatter arc. These sampled states weaken the visual distinction between crawling, zig-zagging and converging.

Some incoming text is behind ORIGINAL's sampled reveal state: 'Where it runs' is dimmer in GPT at 44 seconds, 'Large language models' is fainter at 45 seconds, and 'Vision and speech' has not begun appearing at 46 seconds. The concluding heading is similarly dimmer at 51 seconds.
GPT uses orange accent rules for Recommender systems and Embeddings, where ORIGINAL uses cyan. Its variants note also sits lower, increasing the gap below the six-entry stack.

The final detail shows GPT's terrain ending substantially higher, with a shallower vertical footprint, a lower-looking orange mound and a more exposed grid. ORIGINAL extends farther downward with a deeper curved foreground boundary. Text remains closely positioned, making the terrain mismatch especially apparent.

The detail pairs show heavier-looking GPT serif italics and sans-serif copy, particularly in the opening subtitle, concluding metaphor and lower explanations. Wording and principal line breaks remain close; exact font identity is uncertain.
